reason: The sources provide over 10 well-supported, double-sourced facts detailing the engineering challenges and dramatic sky-crane landing of the Curiosity rover.
story: On November 26, 2011, NASA launched the Mars Science Laboratory aboard an Atlas V rocket, carrying the car-sized Curiosity rover across 352 million miles of space. Previous Mars rovers had bounced onto the surface wrapped in giant inflatable airbags, but at nearly one ton, Curiosity was far too heavy for airbags or traditional landing legs. Instead, engineers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory created an unprecedented entry, descent, and landing system dubbed the seven minutes of terror. After hurtling through the thin Martian atmosphere behind the largest heat shield ever flown and deploying a supersonic parachute, a rocket-powered sky crane descent stage ignited its thrusters. Hovering above Gale Crater on August 6, 2012, the sky crane lowered Curiosity onto its six wheels via cables. The instant touchdown was confirmed, explosive cutters severed the tethers, allowing the sky crane to fly away and crash safely at a distance.
angle: Because Curiosity was too massive for airbags or landing legs, NASA landed the car-sized rover on Mars using a rocket-powered sky crane that lowered it on tethers before flying off to crash.

claims.claim: NASA launched the Mars Science Laboratory mission on November 26, 2011.
The spacecraft launched aboard an Atlas V rocket.
The Curiosity rover traveled approximately 352 million miles to reach Mars.
Curiosity successfully landed on Mars on August 6, 2012 UTC.
Curiosity landed inside Gale Crater on the Martian surface.
At nearly one ton, Curiosity is a car-sized rover.
Curiosity was too heavy to use the airbag landing system deployed on earlier Mars rovers.
Landing signals took approximately 14 minutes to travel from Mars back to Earth.
Curiosity entered the Martian atmosphere using a heat shield and a giant supersonic parachute to slow its descent.
A rocket-powered sky crane lowered Curiosity directly onto its six wheels using cables.
Once Curiosity touched down, explosive cable cutters freed the rover from the sky crane.
After releasing Curiosity, the sky crane flew away to crash-land a safe distance from the rover.
Curiosity is powered by a radioisotope thermoelectric generator utilizing plutonium-238.
Curiosity carries a rock-zapping laser instrument to analyze the chemical composition of Martian rocks.
The primary goal of Curiosity's mission was to evaluate whether Mars ever had conditions capable of supporting microbial life.
Mount Sharp is a 3-mile-high mountain situated in the center of Gale Crater.
The total cost of the Mars Science Laboratory project was approximately 2.5 billion dollars.
Curiosity's touchdown confirmation signal was relayed to Earth via the Mars Odyssey orbiter.

disputed: Tether length during lowering: S1 states 7.6 m (25 ft), S2 states 20 m (66 ft), and S5 states 65 ft. Handle by omitting specific numeric tether length in the script.
Parachute diameter: S1 states 16 m (52 ft), whereas S5 states 65 ft. Handle by describing it generally as a massive supersonic parachute.
Rover weight in pounds: S1/S2 give 1,982 lb (899 kg), whereas S5 states 1,654 lb. Handle by referring to the rover as 'car-sized' or 'one ton'.
